questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following reaction steps is known as propagation step
questions.solution:
In a free radical substitution reaction, the mechanism involves three types of steps:

1. Initiation step: A neutral molecule breaks down to form free radicals.
$\text{Cl-Cl} \rightarrow \text{Cl}^\bullet + \text{Cl}^\bullet$

2. Propagation step: A free radical reacts with a neutral molecule to generate a new free radical and a new neutral molecule. This step keeps the chain reaction going.
$\text{CH}_3^\bullet + \text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{-Cl} + \text{Cl}^\bullet$

3. Termination step: Two free radicals combine to form a neutral molecule, stopping the chain reaction.
$\text{CH}_3^\bullet + \text{Cl}^\bullet \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{-Cl}$
$\text{CH}_3^\bullet + \text{CH}_3^\bullet \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{-CH}_3$

Therefore, the reaction $\text{CH}_3^\bullet + \text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{-Cl} + \text{Cl}^\bullet$ represents the propagation step.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following alkenes on oxidation by $\text{KMnO}_4$ in dil $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ forms adipic acid ?
questions.solution:
Oxidation of alkenes with acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$ leads to the cleavage of the carbon-carbon double bond, converting the vinylic carbons into carboxylic acids, ketones, or $\text{CO}_2$ depending on the substitution.

Cyclohexene is a cyclic alkene with a six-membered ring. Upon oxidative cleavage, the ring opens to form a straight-chain dicarboxylic acid with six carbon atoms.

The reaction is:
Cyclohexene $\xrightarrow{\text{KMnO}_4, \text{H}^+}\text{HOOC}-(\text{CH}_2)_4-\text{COOH}$ (Adipic acid).

Hex-1-ene gives pentanoic acid and $\text{CO}_2$.
Hex-2-ene gives acetic acid and butanoic acid.
Hex-3-ene gives two moles of propanoic acid.

Answer: Cyclohexene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the major product of following reaction.
$\text{Propene} \xrightarrow[\large{\text{Peroxide}}]{\large{\text{HBr}}} \,?$
questions.solution:
The reaction of propene with $HBr$ in the presence of peroxide proceeds via a free radical mechanism, known as the peroxide effect or anti-Markovnikov addition.

The peroxide undergoes homolytic cleavage to form alkoxy radicals, which then abstract a hydrogen atom from $HBr$ to generate a bromine radical (Br^{\bullet}$).

The bromine radical adds to the less substituted carbon atom of the double bond in propene to generate a more stable secondary free radical:

$CH_3-CH=CH_2 + Br^{\bullet} \rightarrow CH_3-\dot{C}H-CH_2Br$

The secondary free radical then abstracts a hydrogen atom from another molecule of $HBr$ to form the final product:

$CH_3-\dot{C}H-CH_2Br + HBr \rightarrow CH_3-CH_2-CH_2Br + Br^{\bullet}$

The major product formed is 1-bromopropane.

Answer: 1 - Bromopropane$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following hydrocarbons has stronger London dispersion forces ?
questions.solution:
London dispersion forces increase with an increase in molecular mass and the surface area of the molecule.

Methane (CH_4$) and ethane (C_2H_6$) have lower molecular masses compared to n-pentane and neo-pentane (C_5H_{12}$), resulting in weaker dispersion forces.

Between n-pentane and neo-pentane, n-pentane is a straight-chain alkane, whereas neo-pentane is highly branched and nearly spherical.

The straight-chain structure of n-pentane provides a larger surface area for intermolecular contact compared to the compact structure of neo-pentane.

Therefore, n-pentane has the strongest London dispersion forces among the given hydrocarbons.

Answer: n-pentane$

questions.q: The major product of the following reaction is
questions.solution:
The given reactant is 3-methylhex-3-ene.

The addition of HI to an alkene is an electrophilic addition reaction that proceeds via the formation of a carbocation intermediate.

First, the electrophile $H^+$ attacks the double bond. This can result in two possible carbocations:
1. Protonation at C-4 yields a tertiary carbocation at C-3.
2. Protonation at C-3 yields a secondary carbocation at C-4.

Since a tertiary carbocation is significantly more stable than a secondary carbocation due to greater hyperconjugation and inductive effects, the reaction proceeds predominantly through the tertiary carbocation at C-3.

Finally, the nucleophile $I^-$ attacks this more stable tertiary carbocation, resulting in the iodine atom attaching to C-3.

The major product formed is 3-iodo-3-methylhexane.

Answer: 3 - iodo - 3 - methylhexane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT terminal alkyne ?
questions.solution:
Terminal alkynes have a triple bond at the end of the carbon chain, meaning at least one hydrogen atom is directly attached to a triply bonded carbon atom (R-C \equiv C-H$).

Ethyne is $H-C \equiv C-H$, which is a terminal alkyne.

Propyne is $CH_3-C \equiv C-H$, which is a terminal alkyne.

But-1-yne is $CH_3-CH_2-C \equiv C-H$, which is a terminal alkyne.

But-2-yne is $CH_3-C \equiv C-CH_3$, where the triple bond is between the second and third carbon atoms. It does not have a hydrogen atom attached to the triply bonded carbon atoms. Thus, it is an internal alkyne, not a terminal alkyne.

Answer: But - 2 - yne$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following alkyl chlorides on Wurtz reaction gives 2, 2, 5, 5- tetramethylhexane ?
questions.solution:
Wurtz reaction involves the coupling of two alkyl halide molecules in the presence of sodium and dry ether to form a symmetrical alkane.

$2\text{R-Cl} + 2\text{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \text{R-R} + 2\text{NaCl}$

The given product is 2,2,5,5-tetramethylhexane. Its structure is $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_3$.

Cleaving the molecule symmetrically at the central $\text{C}-\text{C}$ bond gives two identical alkyl groups, which are neopentyl groups, $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{CH}_2-$.

Therefore, the required alkyl chloride is neopentyl chloride, $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{CH}_2-\text{Cl}$.

Answer: $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{CH}_2-\text{Cl}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the product 'B' in the following reaction
$\text{Toluene} \xrightarrow{\large{\text{Chromyl chloride} / \text{CS}_2}} A \xrightarrow{\large{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+}} B$
questions.solution:
The given reaction is the Etard reaction.

Toluene reacts with chromyl chloride ($\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2$) in a non-polar solvent like $\text{CS}_2$ to form a brown chromium complex $A$.

The chromium complex $A$ on hydrolysis with $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$ gives benzaldehyde $B$.

Therefore, the product $B$ is benzaldehyde.

Answer: Benzaldehyde

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Alkenes on oxidation with $\text{KMnO}_4$ in dil $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ forms
questions.solution:
Alkenes undergo oxidative cleavage when treated with a strong oxidizing agent like $\text{KMnO}_4$ in acidic medium (dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$).

During this reaction, the carbon-carbon double bond is completely cleaved. A $=\text{CH}-$ group is initially oxidized to an aldehyde (alkanal), which is highly susceptible to further oxidation under these conditions and immediately oxidizes to a carboxylic acid (alkanoic acid).

For example:
$\text{R}-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{R}' \xrightarrow{\text{KMnO}_4 / \text{H}^+} \text{R}-\text{COOH} + \text{R}'-\text{COOH}$

Thus, the final stable product formed is an alkanoic acid.

Answer: Alkanoic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When excess of chlorine is used in the chlorination of methane find the major product obtained.
questions.solution:
Chlorination of methane is a free radical substitution reaction.

When an excess of chlorine is used, all the hydrogen atoms of methane are successively replaced by chlorine atoms.

The sequence of reactions is:
$CH_4 + Cl_2 \rightarrow CH_3Cl + HCl$
$CH_3Cl + Cl_2 \rightarrow CH_2Cl_2 + HCl$
$CH_2Cl_2 + Cl_2 \rightarrow CHCl_3 + HCl$
$CHCl_3 + Cl_2 \rightarrow CCl_4 + HCl$

Thus, the final major product obtained is tetrachloromethane (CCl_4$).

Answer: Tetrachloromethane$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the use of Baeyer's reagent by the following.
options: Detecting the presence of carbon carbon double bond.
questions.solution:
Baeyer's reagent is a cold, dilute, alkaline solution of potassium permanganate (KMnO_4$).

It is a strong oxidizing agent, but its primary application in qualitative organic analysis is to test for unsaturation.

When Baeyer's reagent reacts with an organic compound containing a carbon-carbon double bond (alkene) or triple bond (alkyne), the purple colour of the permanganate solution disappears and a brown precipitate of manganese dioxide (MnO_2$) is formed.

Therefore, it is used for detecting the presence of carbon-carbon double bonds.

Answer: Detecting the presence of carbon carbon double bond.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the catalyst used in the Friedel crafts acylation reaction.
questions.solution:
Friedel-Crafts acylation is an electrophilic aromatic substitution reaction in which an acyl group is introduced into an aromatic ring.

The reaction requires a strong Lewis acid catalyst to facilitate the generation of the electrophilic acylium ion from an acyl halide or acid anhydride.

Anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ is the standard and most widely used Lewis acid catalyst for this purpose.

The general reaction is:
$\text{ArH} + \text{RCOCl} \xrightarrow{\text{Anhydrous AlCl}_3} \text{ArCOR} + \text{HCl}$

Answer: Anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following alkanes is NOT obtained when a mixture of ethyl iodide and n-propyl iodide is subjected to Wurtz reaction?
questions.solution:
In the Wurtz reaction, alkyl halides react with sodium in dry ether to form alkanes through the coupling of alkyl radicals.

The given mixture contains ethyl iodide (C_2H_5I$) and n-propyl iodide (C_3H_7I$). The free radicals generated are the ethyl radical (C_2H_5^{\bullet}$) and the n-propyl radical (C_3H_7^{\bullet}$).

The possible coupling products are:
1. Self-coupling of ethyl radicals:
$C_2H_5^{\bullet} + C_2H_5^{\bullet} \rightarrow C_4H_{10}$ (n-Butane)

2. Cross-coupling of ethyl and n-propyl radicals:
$C_2H_5^{\bullet} + C_3H_7^{\bullet} \rightarrow C_5H_{12}$ (n-Pentane)

3. Self-coupling of n-propyl radicals:
$C_3H_7^{\bullet} + C_3H_7^{\bullet} \rightarrow C_6H_{14}$ (n-Hexane)

Propane (C_3H_8$) would require the coupling of a methyl radical (CH_3^{\bullet}$) and an ethyl radical (C_2H_5^{\bullet}$). Since methyl iodide is not present in the mixture, propane is not obtained as a coupling product.

Answer: Propane$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following alkenes is highly stabilized ?
questions.solution:
The stability of an alkene increases with the number of alkyl groups attached to the double-bonded carbon atoms due to hyperconjugation and the +I effect.

The order of stability of alkenes based on substitution is:
Tetrasubstituted > Trisubstituted > Disubstituted > Monosubstituted.

Among the given options, $\text{R}_2\text{C}=\text{CR}_2$ is a tetrasubstituted alkene, having the maximum number of alkyl groups attached to the double bond. Thus, it has the maximum number of hyperconjugative structures and is the most highly stabilized alkene.

Answer: $\text{R}_2\text{C} = \text{CR}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What are the reactants involved in Friedal Crafts alkylation?
questions.solution:
Friedel-Crafts alkylation is an electrophilic aromatic substitution reaction in which an alkyl group is introduced into an aromatic ring.

The typical reactants are an aromatic compound, such as benzene ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_6$), and an alkyl halide, such as methyl chloride ($\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$). The reaction is carried out in the presence of a Lewis acid catalyst like anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$.

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + \text{CH}_3\text{Cl} \xrightarrow{\text{Anhydrous AlCl}_3} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_3 + \text{HCl}$

The reaction of benzene with acetyl chloride ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCl}$) corresponds to Friedel-Crafts acylation.

Thus, the reactants involved in Friedel-Crafts alkylation are $\text{C}_6\text{H}_6$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$.

Answer: $\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + \text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the product of reforming reaction of n-hexane in the presence of $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$ over alumina.
questions.solution:
Alkanes containing six or more carbon atoms on heating to $773 \text{ K}$ at $10-20 \text{ atm}$ pressure in the presence of oxides of vanadium, molybdenum or chromium supported over alumina get dehydrogenated and cyclised to benzene and its homologues. This reaction is known as aromatization or reforming.

When n-hexane is passed over $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$ supported on alumina, it undergoes aromatization to form benzene.

$\text{CH}_3-(\text{CH}_2)_4-\text{CH}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{V}_2\text{O}_5 / \text{Al}_2\text{O}_3, 773 \text{ K}, 10-20 \text{ atm}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + 4\text{H}_2$

Answer: Benzene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When a mixture of two different alkyl halides reacts with metallic sodium in dry ether, the formation of a possible number of alkanes are-
questions.solution:
Let the two different alkyl halides be $R-X$ and $R'-X$.

When this mixture reacts with metallic sodium in dry ether (Wurtz reaction), three types of coupling reactions take place.

$R-X + 2Na + X-R \rightarrow R-R + 2NaX$

$R'-X + 2Na + X-R' \rightarrow R'-R' + 2NaX$

$R-X + 2Na + X-R' \rightarrow R-R' + 2NaX$

Thus, a total of three different alkanes are formed.

Answer: Three

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following compound will show addition of HBr to alkene according to markownikoff's rule?
questions.solution:
Markovnikov's rule is applicable for the addition of unsymmetrical reagents to unsymmetrical alkenes.

But-2-ene ($CH_3-CH=CH-CH_3$) is a symmetrical alkene.

Hex-3-ene ($CH_3-CH_2-CH=CH-CH_2-CH_3$) is a symmetrical alkene.

Ethene ($CH_2=CH_2$) is a symmetrical alkene.

2-methylpropene ($CH_3-C(CH_3)=CH_2$) is an unsymmetrical alkene.

Therefore, 2-methylpropene will undergo addition of HBr according to Markovnikov's rule.

questions.q: Identify the compound formed when But-2-ene is treated with $\text{KMnO}_4$ in dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$.
questions.solution:
But-2-ene has the structure $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3$.

When treated with acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$ ($\text{KMnO}_4$ in dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$), it undergoes oxidative cleavage. The strong oxidizing agent completely breaks the carbon-carbon double bond, oxidizing each of the resulting fragments into a carboxylic acid.

$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{KMnO}_4, \text{H}^+} 2 \text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$

The product formed is acetic acid (ethanoic acid).

Answer: Acetic acid

questions.q: What is the product of decarboxylation of anhydrous sodium benzoate?
questions.solution:
Decarboxylation of anhydrous sodium benzoate is carried out by heating it with soda lime, which is a mixture of sodium hydroxide and calcium oxide.

The reaction proceeds as follows:

$C_6H_5COONa + NaOH \xrightarrow{CaO, \Delta} C_6H_6 + Na_2CO_3$

The main product formed in this reaction is benzene.

Answer: Benzene

The Etard reaction involves the oxidation of a methyl group attached to an aromatic ring (such as toluene) to an aldehyde group (such as benzaldehyde).

The reagent used for this specific transformation is chromyl chloride (CrO_2Cl_2$) in a non-polar solvent like $CS_2$ or $CCl_4$, followed by hydrolysis.

The reaction proceeds via the formation of a brown chromium complex, which upon decomposition with water yields the corresponding aldehyde.

Answer: Chromyl chloride$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds does not decolourise $\text{Br}_2$ water?
questions.solution:
Bromine water test is used to detect the presence of unsaturation (double or triple bonds) in organic compounds.

Alkenes and alkynes undergo electrophilic addition reactions with bromine water, leading to the decolourisation of the reddish-brown colour of bromine.

Ethene, ethyne, and cyclohexene are unsaturated compounds and thus readily decolourise bromine water.

Benzene is an aromatic compound and is highly stable due to resonance. It does not undergo addition reactions under normal conditions and therefore does not decolourise bromine water.

Answer: Benzene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $200$ mL of ethylene gas and $150$ mL of HCl gas were allowed to react at $1$ bar. Pressure to form gaseous ethyl chloride. What is the work done during the reaction?
questions.solution:
The balanced chemical equation for the reaction is:

$C_2H_4(g) + HCl(g) \rightarrow C_2H_5Cl(g)$

Initial volumes:
$V_{C_2H_4} = 200$ mL
$V_{HCl} = 150$ mL

Total initial volume $V_i = 200 + 150 = 350$ mL.

Since the reaction occurs at constant pressure and temperature, the volumes of gases are directly proportional to their number of moles. Here, $HCl$ is the limiting reagent.

Volume of $C_2H_4$ reacted = $150$ mL
Volume of $C_2H_4$ remaining = $200 - 150 = 50$ mL
Volume of $C_2H_5Cl$ formed = $150$ mL

Total final volume $V_f = 50 + 150 = 200$ mL.

Change in volume $\Delta V = V_f - V_i = 200 - 350 = -150$ mL = $-0.15$ L.

The work done during the reaction at constant pressure is given by:

$W = -P \Delta V$

Substituting the values:

$W = -1 \text{ bar} \times (-0.15 \text{ L}) = 0.15 \text{ L bar}$

Since $1 \text{ L bar} = 100 \text{ J}$, we get:

$W = 0.15 \times 100 \text{ J} = 15 \text{ J}$

Answer: $15$ J

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following types of reactions is used to prepare Alkyl benzene?
questions.solution:
The Wurtz-Fittig reaction involves the reaction of an aryl halide with an alkyl halide in the presence of sodium metal and dry ether to form an alkyl benzene.

$C_6H_5X + RX + 2Na \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} C_6H_5R + 2NaX$

Swartz reaction is used for the synthesis of alkyl fluorides.

Sandmeyer reaction is used to synthesize aryl halides from aryl diazonium salts.

Finkelstein reaction is used for the preparation of alkyl iodides from alkyl chlorides or bromides.

Answer: Wurtz Fittig reaction

questions.q: Cyclohexene on oxidation by $\text{KMnO}_4$ in dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ produces
questions.solution:

When treated with a strong oxidizing agent like $\text{KMnO}_4$ in an acidic medium (dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$), the carbon-carbon double bond undergoes oxidative cleavage.

The product is $\text{HOOC}-(\text{CH}_2)_4-\text{COOH}$, which is hexane-1,6-dioic acid (commonly known as adipic acid).

Answer: hexane-1,6-dioic acid

questions.solution:
Benzene is a known human carcinogen and is highly toxic. Prolonged exposure to benzene can lead to severe health issues, including leukemia and other blood-related diseases.

Alkanes, alkenes, and alkynes in their simple forms are generally not considered carcinogenic.

Answer: Benzene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following is obtained as major product when methoxybenzene is treated with nitrating mixture?
questions.solution:
Methoxybenzene (anisole) undergoes electrophilic aromatic substitution when treated with a nitrating mixture (conc. $\text{HNO}_3$ and conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$).

The $-\text{OCH}_3$ group is an electron-donating group through the $+R$ effect, which increases the electron density at the ortho and para positions of the benzene ring. Thus, it acts as an ortho, para-directing group.

Nitration of methoxybenzene yields a mixture of 2-nitroanisole (ortho product) and 4-nitroanisole (para product).

Due to steric hindrance at the ortho position caused by the bulky methoxy group, the para product, 4-nitroanisole, is formed as the major product.

Answer: 4-Nitroanisole

Methane reacts with chlorine under UV light through free radical substitution. The stepwise mechanism involves:

Each former alkene carbon forms a carboxylic acid group, with the four methylene groups connecting them: $\mathrm{Cyclohexene} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{KMnO}_4/\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4} \mathrm{HOOC}\unicode{8211}(\mathrm{CH}_2)_4\unicode{8211}\mathrm{COOH}$.

questions.q: What is the difference in molar mases of third and fourth homologues of alkane series?
questions.solution:
The general formula for alkanes is $C_nH_{2n+2}$.

The third homologue corresponds to $n = 3$, yielding propane $C_3H_8$. The molar mass is calculated as $(3 \times 12) + (8 \times 1) = 44$ g/mol.

For the fourth homologue at $n = 4$, the formula is butane $C_4H_{10}$, with molar mass $(4 \times 12) + (10 \times 1) = 58$ g/mol.

The difference is $58 - 44 = 14$ g/mol. This matches the mass of a $CH_2$ unit (12 + 2 = 14$ g/mol), which is the constant increment between successive homologues in any homologous series.

Final answer: 14$ g/mol

options: Alkanes with less then 10 Carbon atoms
Alkanes having 20 C to 25 C atoms

questions.solution:
Alkane Properties and Uses by Carbon Chain Length

Gaseous alkanes (C1–C4) serve primarily as fuels, including methane in natural gas and propane/butane in liquefied petroleum gas (LPG).

Liquid alkanes (C5–C17) are key components of gasoline, kerosene, and diesel fuels.

Waxy solid alkanes (C18–C35) appear in paraffin wax, lubricating oils, and greases.

Higher molecular weight alkanes (over C35) are viscous liquids or solids used chiefly in bitumen for road surfacing and roofing applications.

Thus, alkanes with more than 35 carbon atoms are employed for road surfacing.

The correct option is D.

questions.solution:
Hydroboration-oxidation of propene proceeds through anti-Markovnikov addition of water across the double bond.

The reaction begins with hydroboration, where the boron atom adds to the less substituted carbon while hydrogen adds to the more substituted carbon. Propene reacts with borane to form tri-$n$-propylborane: $3\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 + \text{BH}_3 \rightarrow (\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2)_3\text{B}$.

Oxidation with alkaline hydrogen peroxide cleaves the boron-carbon bonds, replacing boron with hydroxyl groups: $(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2)_3\text{B} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}_2 + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow 3\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + \text{Na}_3\text{BO}_3$.

The product is propan-1-ol, with the hydroxyl group on the terminal carbon. Tri-$n$-propylborane is an intermediate, tri-iso-propylborane would result from Markovnikov addition, and propan-2-ol forms through acid-catalyzed hydration.

The correct choice is $\boxed{\text{C}}$.

The secondary radical, $\mathrm{CH_3 CH\cdot CH_3 }$, is more stable than the primary radical due to hyperconjugation and inductive effects. Bromination is highly selective, favoring formation of the more stable radical with lower activation energy.

Thus, 2-bromopropane forms predominantly.

$\mathrm{CH_3 CH\cdot CH_3 + Br_2 \rightarrow CH_3 CHBrCH_3 + Br\cdot}$

The major product is 2-bromopropane.

Analysis of options: Cyclohexanol arises from hydration; cyclohexanone from milder oxidation or ozonolysis with reduction; hexanoic acid is monocarboxylic. Adipic acid is the dicarboxylic product consistent with strong oxidative cleavage.

questions.q: The reaction of aryl halide with sodium metal in dry ether to give biphenyl is known as
questions.solution:
The reaction of aryl halides with sodium metal in dry ether to form biphenyl constitutes the Fittig reaction. This transformation produces biaryl compounds through the general reaction $\mathrm{Ar-X + 2Na + X-Ar \rightarrow Ar-Ar + 2NaX}$.

The Swartz reaction employs metallic fluorides to synthesize alkyl fluorides and does not involve aryl halides or biphenyl formation. The Wurtz reaction couples two alkyl halides to form alkanes: $\mathrm{R-X + 2Na + X-R \rightarrow R-R + 2NaX}$.

Although the Wurtz-Fittig reaction involves aryl halides, it requires an alkyl halide co-reactant and produces alkylarenes rather than biaryls.

Since the transformation specifically couples two aryl halide molecules to form a biaryl compound, it corresponds exclusively to the Fittig reaction.

Alkane Properties and Uses by Carbon Chain Length

Gaseous alkanes (C1–C4) serve primarily as fuels, including methane in natural gas and propane/butane in liquefied petroleum gas (LPG).

Liquid alkanes (C5–C17) are key components of gasoline, kerosene, and diesel fuels.

Waxy solid alkanes (C18–C35) appear in paraffin wax, lubricating oils, and greases.

Higher molecular weight alkanes (over C35) are viscous liquids or solids used chiefly in bitumen for road surfacing and roofing applications.

Thus, alkanes with more than 35 carbon atoms are employed for road surfacing.

The correct option is D.

questions.q: Identify the major product formed when 2-Methylhexan-3-ol is heated with concentrated sulphuric acid.
questions.solution:
Dehydration of 2-methylhexan-3-ol with concentrated $\mathrm{H_2 SO_4}$ proceeds via an E1 mechanism. Protonation of the hydroxyl group forms an oxonium ion, which loses water to yield a secondary carbocation at C3.

To enhance stability, a 1,2-hydride shift occurs from the adjacent carbon, converting the secondary carbocation into a tertiary carbocation at C2: $\mathrm{CH_3-C+(CH_3)-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3}$.

Elimination follows Zaitsev's rule, favoring formation of the most substituted alkene. Deprotonation from C3 generates the trisubstituted alkene 2-methylhex-2-ene: $\mathrm{CH_3-C(CH_3)=CH-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3}$, which corresponds to option A.

The final answer is $\boxed{A}$.

questions.q: How many gram of sodium (atomic mass 23 u) is required to prepare one mole of ethane from methyl chloride by Wurtz reaction?
questions.solution:
The Wurtz reaction between methyl chloride and sodium metal in presence of dry ether can be written as:
$2C{H}_{3} + Cl + 2Na\overset{Dryether}{\to}C{H}_{3}\mathop{-}_{Ethane}C{H}_{3} + 2NaCl$
$⇒$ moles of sodium metal reacts to give 1 mole of ethane.
Also,
1 mole of Na metal $= 23g$
$∴ 2 moles of Na metal $= 23 \times 2 = 46g$
Thus, 46 g of sodium is required to prepare one mole of ethane from methyl chloride by Wurtz reaction.$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The reactions of alkanes are explosive with which halogen?
questions.solution:
The reaction of alkanes with fluorine is difficult to control bacause the activation energy for hydrogen abstraction is so low.
The initiation step involves the homolytic cleavage of the $F - F$ bond.
$F - F \to \overset{.}{F} + \overset{.}{F} ; {E}_{a} = + 155kJ / mol$
This is a high activation energy. But only a few $F$ atoms need to form.
Each $F$ atom can then initiate thousands of propagation steps.
$C{H}_{4} + \overset{.}{F} \to C{H}_{3} F + \overset{.}{H}$
These steps are highly exothermic; $\Delta H^{o} = - 431kJ / mol.$
